name: Citizenship by Grant (Naturalisation)

requirements.blocker_text: Must have been living as a New Zealand resident (holding a Resident Visa or Permanent Resident Visa) for at least the last 5 years.

Physically present in New Zealand for a minimum of 1,350 days during the 5 years immediately preceding the application, including at least 240 days in each of 12 of the 60 months -- these exact day figures are confirmed only by tier-3 legal-commentary sources, not stated numerically on the tier-1 govt.nz overview pages reviewed in this pass.
Must be able to hold a basic conversation in English.
Must intend to continue living in New Zealand.

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: 1,350 days within the preceding 5 years, incl. 240+ days in each of 12 months

sources.title: New Zealand Government (govt.nz) -- Requirements for NZ citizenship: 5-year residence, conversational English, good character, intent to remain; notes a citizenship test will be introduced for most applicants from late 2027 (not yet in force)
Duncan Cotterill (NZ law firm) -- New Zealand citizenship: exact presence-day figures (1,350 days over 5 years; 240 days in each of 12 months), Ministerial discretion for exceptional circumstances

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (New Zealand). dual_citizenship_allowed modeled TRUE -- New Zealand imposes no renunciation requirement, unlike several other countries in this dataset. A citizenship TEST (beyond the existing conversational-English and character checks) is confirmed by the tier-1 source to be introduced for most applicants from LATE 2027 -- NOT YET IN FORCE as of this verified_at date, so not modeled as a current requirement, consistent with this dataset's live-reform handling convention (see Finland's citizenship-test precedent). The Minister of Internal Affairs retains discretion to grant citizenship in exceptional circumstances to applicants who do not meet all standard criteria, per the tier-3 source -- not modeled as a separate route given its fully discretionary, non-criteria-based nature.
